text:
anya: hey team, noticed a pathological case with multi-hop requests where backpressure signals vanish and high-priority streams starve lower-priority long-polls
ben: can you paste an example trace?
anya: sure — 3 hops: frontdoor -> regional-proxy -> egress. frontdoor drops on overload, regional queues backlog, egress keeps accepting. result: long-poll clients never get tokens because frontdoor stops issuing grant frames
mohit: is this the case where request-level tokens are only kept on the ingress side?
anya: exactly. we only propagate an accept/queue decision, not the dynamic queue depth or aging. so later hops assume client is low priority
sam: proposal: attach a compact priority-age header on initial request and let each hop increment age when the request gets queued. use age to boost effective priority downstream
li: +1 for age, but we gotta avoid header bloat and replay problems. maybe a single byte where bits are: ttl, age-sat, reserved?
ben: practical encoding: X-Pri-Age: basePriority|ageTicks e.g. "p=5;a=3". each hop increments a up to 15. weight = basePriority + floor(a * ageBoost)
mohit: what about malicious clients hacking header to set age high? we need hop-signed or hop-validated tokens. could sign with frontdoor ephemeral key and downstream validate signature; downside: crypto overhead
anya: or only accept age deltas from trusted hops — the first hop stamps a short-lived HMAC (header + timestamp) and routers only accept increments from peers in our AS with shared key
sam: fallback if signature missing: treat age as 0 (conservative). makes attackers lose advantage
li: algorithmic behavior question: how does boosting affect token-bucket fairness? if we boost too aggressively, old low-priority requests will overtake active high-priority transient bursts
ben: we can compute effectiveWeight = basePriority * (1 + age * alpha) where alpha is small (0.05). also add per-tenant cap so single tenant can't monopolize aged boosts
mohit: also need admission control: each hop should expose two paths: fast-pass (no queue) and queued path. when queued, increment age tick and attach queue-depth hint header: X-Queue-Depth: 42
anya: queue-depth helps downstream make admission decisions without reading full queues. but it's approximated and risks oscillation
li: agree, add randomized smoothing: hop reports exponential decayed queue depth. header is noisy but useful
sam: implementation detail: we should avoid per-request DB lookups. keep all logic in the proxy fast-path. store per-tenant counters in local sharded memcache cluster if needed
ben: what about streaming responses where we can't easily reclassify mid-stream? e.g., a streaming generation that gets queued mid-flight
anya: for streaming, we can snapshot priority at the start and allow mid-flight priority nudges via trailer metadata: X-Stream-Priority-Delta: +1. proxies can decide to accelerate flushes if bandwidth available
mohit: tradeoff: adding trailers requires ensuring client and protocol support (HTTP/2 trailers or gRPC). for websocket/long-lived connections we can use control frames
li: operational concern: how do we surface this in observability? we should tag traces with finalEffectivePriority and ageTicks, and add histogram of age at egress vs latency
anya: agree — add SLIs: fraction of requests with age>3, median latency by age bucket, per-tenant starvation alerts
sam: rollout plan: 1) header-only no-auth PoC in staging for internal traffic; 2) HMAC signing and validation on internal infra; 3) enable queue-depth hints; 4) streaming trailers for gRPC routes
ben: backward compatibility: if a hop doesn't understand headers, it just ignores them. but that means we need >=2 hop rollout in region to be effective
mohit: perf ballpark: header parsing + increment is ~50ns on path if code inline (no allocation). signing is heavier ~200-400us but only done at first hop
li: security note: make sure we rotate HMAC keys and limit TTL to a few seconds to avoid replay over multi-second queues
anya: open questions: should age decay if the request is unqueued for a while (i.e., time-based rather than tick-based)? ticks are simpler for small queues but time-aware might be fairer
sam: time-based: age = floor((now - firstQueueTs) / 200ms) — needs monotonic timestamps from each hop and consistent clock. risk: clock skew. ticks avoids that
anya: leaning ticks to start, and later experiment with hybrid if we see starvation
mohit: can we simulate with the loadgen? I'll add a scenario with mixed priorities and exponential arrivals
ben: please include tenant caps and alpha config defaults in the RFC. also define what counts as "queued" (enqueued to worker vs immediate accept)
li: small UX: add new metric names: redwood.edge.priority.age_ticks and redwood.edge.queue.depth_hint
anya: thanks — I'll draft the mini-RFC with algorithm, header format, HMAC sketch, rollout steps, and observability plan.
deploy-bot: note: canary proxy image redwood/proxy:vnext-rc1 deployed to staging-us-west at 1790012355 :rocket:
ben: nice, can we wire a smoke that asserts headers are propagated through 3-hop path?
anya: yes, adding that to the test matrix
sam: ack, will watch the canary and kick off loadgen once PoC landed
li: if no objections by EOD, I'll merge the RFC branch to drafts repo
anya: no objections from me. thanks all :thumbsup:
